original_value: Brain tumors are one of the most deadly diseases with a high mortality rate. The shape and size of the tumor are random during the growth process. Brain tumor segmentation is a brain tumor assisted diagnosis technology that separates different brain tumor structures such as edema and active and tumor necrosis tissues from normal brain tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology has the advantages of no radiation impact on the human body, good imaging effect on structural tissues, and an ability to realize tomographic imaging of any orientation. Therefore, doctors often use MRI brain tumor images to analyze and process brain tumors. In these images, the tumor structure is only characterized by grayscale changes, and the developed images obtained by different equipment and different conditions may also be different. This makes it difficult for traditional image segmentation methods to deal well with the segmentation of brain tumor images. Considering that the traditional single-mode MRI brain tumor images contain incomplete brain tumor information, it is difficult to segment the single-mode brain tumor images to meet clinical needs. In this paper, a sparse subspace clustering (SSC) algorithm is introduced to process the diagnosis of multimodal MRI brain tumor images. In the absence of added noise, the proposed algorithm has better advantages than traditional methods. Compared with the top 15 in the Brats 2015 competition, the accuracy is not much different, being basically stable between 10 and 15. In order to verify the noise resistance of the proposed algorithm, this paper adds 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% Gaussian noise to the test image. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has better noise immunity than a comparable algorithm.

result.paraphrase: Brain tumors are among the most lethal diseases, with a high mortality rate. During growth, tumor shape and size are random. Brain tumor segmentation is an assisted diagnostic technique that separates structures such as edema, active tumor, and necrotic tissue from normal brain tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has the advantages of no radiation exposure to the human body, good imaging of structural tissues, and the ability to perform tomographic imaging in any orientation. For this reason, doctors often use MRI brain tumor images to analyze and process brain tumors. In these images, the tumor is reflected only by grayscale variations, and images acquired by different devices and under different conditions may also differ. This makes it difficult for traditional image segmentation methods to segment brain tumor images effectively. Since conventional single-mode MRI brain tumor images contain incomplete tumor information, it is hard to segment single-mode brain tumor images to meet clinical needs. This paper introduces a sparse subspace clustering (SSC) algorithm for diagnosing multimodal MRI brain tumor images. Without added noise, the proposed algorithm performs better than traditional methods. Compared with the top 15 methods in the BraTS 2015 competition, its accuracy is not significantly different and is basically stable between 10 and 15. To verify the noise resistance of the proposed algorithm, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% Gaussian noise are added to the test images. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has stronger noise immunity than a comparable algorithm.
